article.headline: Games To Watch: Olive Branch takes unbeaten starts on the road; North Pike visits Florence
article.html:
Olive Branch puts unbeaten girls and boys basketball starts on the road Saturday, while North Pike visits Florence with winning records in both varsity divisions. Those matchups lead the remaining November 21, 2026, slate, with boys soccer offering an additional Northeast Mississippi connection through Corinth and Amory.

This Games To Watch selection covers upcoming varsity games whose dates and start times were verified before publication. All times are Central Standard Time. Records are the entering figures listed on the individual matchup pages; completed games and contests already underway are excluded.

Olive Branch sends unbeaten basketball teams on the road

Olive Branch’s girls enter the 4:30 p.m. game at Columbus at 2–0. Columbus is listed at 1–3, making this a chance for the Falcons to challenge an unbeaten opponent at home. For the Conquistadors, the nonconference trip offers another test of a perfect opening away from their own floor.

The boys face a different opponent: Olive Branch visits Starkville at 6 p.m. with a matching 2–0 record. The Yellowjackets enter 2–3. The records put the immediate opportunity in clear terms—Olive Branch can protect its unbeaten start, while Starkville can move back to an even record by winning at home. This game is also listed as nonconference.

For more coverage involving Olive Branch and other Mississippi schools, see our latest statewide scores roundup.

North Pike and Florence meet at the Thanksgiving Classic

The 6 p.m. girls game brings together North Pike at 4–1 and Florence at 3–1. Both have winning starts with only one reported defeat, giving this matchup more balance on paper than a meeting between an unbeaten team and a struggling opponent. The fixture is listed as part of the Florence Thanksgiving Classic.

North Pike’s boys also enter 4–1 for the 7:30 p.m. meeting with Florence, which is listed at 1–2. The Eagles have an opportunity to even their record, while the Jaguars can build on a start that already includes several wins. The boys fixture is identified as a tournament game at the same Thanksgiving Classic.

Columbus and Northwest Rankin bring winning records

Columbus hosts Northwest Rankin in a 7:30 p.m. boys basketball game pairing the Falcons’ 4–1 record with the Cougars’ 3–2 start. Each team has more wins than losses entering the nonconference meeting. For Columbus, the attraction is the opportunity to extend a strong opening against another winning opponent; Northwest Rankin can strengthen its own early record on the road.

Kosciusko’s boys protect a perfect start

Kosciusko’s girls are listed at 3–1 ahead of the 6 p.m. game against Holmes County Central. The visiting Jaguars enter 1–5. The Whippets can build on an opening with only one loss, while Holmes County Central has a chance to improve a difficult early record against a winning team.

The 7:30 p.m. boys game gives Kosciusko an unbeaten record to defend. The Whippets enter 3–0 and Holmes County Central is listed at 0–6. Both varsity games are nonconference, with the boys matchup offering the visitors a chance to earn their first reported win while trying to hand Kosciusko its first defeat.

Soccer: Corinth at Richland, Amory at Pass Christian

Corinth’s boys meet Richland at 4:30 p.m. in a nonconference soccer match. The Warriors enter with a listed 2–5–1 record and Richland is 2–6–2. With neither team carrying a winning record into the fixture, the match offers an opportunity to add a needed victory rather than defend a perfect start.

Amory brings the stronger entering record to its 5:45 p.m. boys match at Pass Christian. The Panthers are listed at 5–2 and the Pirates at 3–4–1. That contrast makes the nonconference meeting worth following: Amory can extend a winning opening away from home, while Pass Christian can draw level in wins and losses by beating a winning opponent.

Jackson Academy visits Choctaw Central

Another girls basketball option is Jackson Academy at Choctaw Central at 4:30 p.m.. The Raiders enter 2–2 and the Warriors 3–4. Jackson Academy can move above the break-even mark, while Choctaw Central can reach it. The matchup is listed as nonconference, with both teams seeking a result that changes the balance of their early records.
